summary: George Berrington led the retention and expansion session with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley. Elmstead's client list shows 31 clients in three years but only 6 bought a second programme. We agreed to name six key accounts, introduce a close-out review on every programme and pursue follow-on phases before the first phase ends.

discussion.keyPoints: Kate's list showed 31 clients and 6 repeat buyers. Andrew said the firm tends to finish a programme and walk away because consultants move straight to the next bid.
George asked which clients could realistically spend over 500k in two years. Kate named four water utilities and two integrated care boards.
There is no formal feedback. Andrew worried that asking for scores in the public sector could be awkward.

recommendations.recommendation: Name six key accounts, four water utilities and two integrated care boards, each with a partner owner and an account plan.
Propose a follow-on phase at least eight weeks before every programme ends.
Run a close-out review with the senior responsible owner on every programme, with a simple 1 to 10 score.
Ask every satisfied client for a reference call agreement rather than a named case study.
Set a repeat-client target of 40 percent of revenue.

actions.action: Write account plans for the six key accounts

nextFocus: Build the financial model behind fixed fees, bid costs and the shift away from tenders.
nextPreparation: Andrew to bring utilisation, day rates and bid cost data for the last 12 months.

tests.question: Which clients are our key accounts?
Is the close-out review with a satisfaction score agreed?
When should we propose a follow-on phase?
